title: Non-Inverting Op-Amp: A Voltage Divider Sets the Gain
topic: Non-inverting op-amp configuration — V_in at V+, R1 to ground, R_f from V_out to V−; virtual short forces V− = V_in, so V_out = (1 + R_f/R1)·V_in; gain is positive and always ≥ 1

beats.narration: Same op-amp — but this time drive the plus pin. What does the output do?

elements.content: Drive V+, see what comes out.

beats.narration: The non-inverting configuration: V in feeds the plus pin directly. R 1 ties V minus to ground; R f closes the feedback loop from the output back to V minus.

elements.content: Op-amp triangle pointing right; V_in wire into V+ pin (top of triangle); V- pin connected via R1 to ground and via R_f to V_out; ground symbol at the bottom
Labels: V_in, V+, V−, R1, R_f, V_out, ground
input on V+, feedback through the R1/R_f divider

beats.narration: Negative feedback drags V minus up until it matches V plus. So V minus equals V in — a virtual short, but at V in instead of ground.

elements.content: Same circuit with a pulsing ring around the V− node showing it being tugged to V_in's level
Annotation V_in = V+ = V− painted on the inputs

beats.narration: Now R 1 and R f form a divider from V out down to ground, with V minus tapped between them. Solve V minus equals V out times R 1 over R 1 plus R f, and you get the gain: one plus R f over R 1.

elements.content: Schematic with the R1/R_f voltage divider highlighted between V_out and ground, V_in tapped at the V− node
gain is always at least 1 — and the sign is positive

beats.narration: Sweep V in — V out follows in phase, just bigger.

elements.content: Scope panel: V_in sinusoid in chalk, V_out sinusoid in amber at 2x amplitude, in phase (no inversion); time cursor sweeps left to right
in phase, scaled by 1 + R_f / R1
